subject: Clarifying subprocessor notice timing, e-sign handback, and exception roles
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question on subprocessor notice windows + eSign timing

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week — very helpful. Legal has one operational question before we sign: our procurement team needs clarity on how Redwood handles subprocessor additions and the associated notice window / objection process. Specifically:

- What is the standard notice window for new subprocessors (calendar days)?
- If an exception is required for a payment processor or analytics vendor, how long does Redwood require to implement the exception and what is the approval path?
- We use DocuSign for DPA execution — what is the expected handback timeline after both parties sign (how quickly will the executed copy + subprocessor list be available)?

If you can point me to the standard playbook or provide a short timeline we can include in our SOW, that would be great.

Best,
Alex Mercer
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Analytics
alex.mercer@acmeanalytics.com

(On Acme's side: Lisa Chan (legal) is copied on follow-ups.)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@acmeanalytics.com>, Amelia Wright <amelia@brightlaw.com>, Lisa Chan <lisa.chan@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Question on subprocessor notice windows + eSign timing

Team — looping you in to confirm our standard approach and flag any exceptions. Alex — paraphrasing Acme's asks above.

My proposed answers (draft for legal ops):
- Default notice window: 30 calendar days for routine infra and analytics subprocessors.
- Exceptions: 45-day notice for any payment processors, identity providers, or vendors that handle payment/auth data. Exceptions require Security + Legal sign-off; ops to maintain a short approval queue.
- DocuSign process: Once both parties e-sign the DPA, DocuSign will generate the executed PDF immediately. Redwood target: publish executed DPA + current subprocessor list to the Acme contract folder within 48 hours and log the change in the audit register.

Karthik — can you confirm ops can live with the 45-day carve for payment processors (we previously had 30/45 split in the onboarding checklist). Marissa — can you attach the updated e-sign flow and the checklist you referenced in the last vendor negotiation? Naomi — we'll need audit logging + CRM ticket updates.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Manager, Partnerships & GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com

Jordan / team — Ops can accept the 30/45-day split as a default. A few practical notes:

- 30 days covers most infra/analytics KPIs and gives us standard remediation time.
- 45 days for payment/auth vendors makes sense; we will treat these as "sensitive processors" and route them through priority approval. Approval typically requires a security review + finance check (2–3 business days) but we should call out that any custom onboarding work by the subprocessor (e.g., bespoke connectivity) may extend timelines.
- For emergency/regulatory-required removals we maintain a rapid-removal path but Acme should expect fallback routing while we migrate workloads.

I'll update the Ops checklist and mark the fields that trigger a 45-day review (vendor category, data types, payment token handling).

Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 4 Feb 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Question on subprocessor notice windows + eSign timing

Thanks — attaching the operational artifacts for Acme's legal review. See attachments: DPA_redline_v3.docx (highlights: notice windows, objection workflow, fallback routing) and Subprocessor_Thresholds.xlsx (vendor categories + default notice windows).

Key items to call out for the DPA language: 
- We propose a 30-day published notice with a 45-day exception for payment/auth vendors. The 45-day exception is written as a category-based carve and requires written approval from Redwood Security & Finance.
- Objection process: customer must provide a written objection within the notice period with reasonable detail; we will engage remediation or offer an alternative subprocessor. If unresolved, the contract provides a 60-day transition period before termination rights can be exercised.
- DocuSign handback: we will send the executed PDF to the contract folder and mark the HubSpot deal as "Executed" within 48 hours.

Operational handoff (DocuSign specifics):
1) Legal uploads final DPA to DocuSign and adds Acme signers.
2) Acme signs; DocuSign routes back to Redwood Legal for final signature.
3) DocuSign auto-generates executed PDF; Legal will confirm via email and Ops will update the subprocessor registry.

If BrightLaw (Amelia) has redlines, please comment in DPA_redline_v3 and we will reconcile in a single round to keep the e-sign window under 5 business days.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_redline_v3.docx (see inline comments), Subprocessor_Thresholds.xlsx
